newsitem.title: USA: U.S. census: nearly 10 million kids lack insurance.
newsitem.headline: U.S. census: nearly 10 million kids lack insurance.

text.p: Nearly 10 million children, or close to 14 percent of Americans under age 18, lack health insurance, according to census data released on Thursday.
The Census Bureau found that the uninsured rate was by far the highest among Hispanic children at 26.8 percent. In contrast, the rate for blacks was 15.3 percent, and 13.4 percent for whites.

The data is from 1995, the most recent available. The Census Bureau found that 9.8 million children, or 13.8 percent, had no insurance at all. The rate was slightly higher for teen-agers than for young children.

Just more than 66 percent of youths got their insurance through a privately-purchased or employment-based health plan, and slightly less than one in four were on Medicaid. Minority children were more likely to be on Medicaid, a state-federal health insurance program for the poor, disabled and elderly.
President Bill Clinton's 1998 budget proposal calls for expanding coverage to as many as five million kids, partly through an outreach program to uninsured children who are eligible for Medicaid.

Senate Democrats have said expanding health insurance to children up to age 18 is their No. 1 health priority. Legislation has been introduced in Congress to expand coverage either through tax credits or vouchers parents could use to buy insurance.
Republicans have said they also want to expand coverage, but want to find a market-based way to help children.
